# @stackline/wcwidth@1.0.0

Alexandro.Net documents `@stackline/wcwidth@1.0.0`, an independently maintained,
dependency-free compatibility continuation of `wcwidth@1.0.1`.

## Package identity

- Documentation: https://alexandro.net/docs/vanilla/wcwidth/
- Source: https://github.com/alexandroit/stackline-wcwidth
- License: MIT with original wcwidth and Unicode attribution
- Runtime: Node.js 18 or newer; modern browser bundlers
- Production graph: one node, zero runtime, optional, peer, or bundled dependencies

## API contract

The CommonJS root is a callable `wcwidth` function with arity one. Its `config`
property is enumerable; the additive `unicodeVersion` reference is
non-enumerable. Native ESM provides an equivalent standalone function as its
default plus named `config` and `unicodeVersion` exports.
Conditional declarations cover CommonJS, ESM, TypeScript 3.9, and current
TypeScript.

The default configuration is `{ nul: 0, control: 0 }`. As in the upstream
package, `config(options)` fills missing properties on the supplied object,
observes inherited values, and retains the object so later mutation affects the
configured function.

## Unicode model

Checksum-pinned Unicode 17.0.0 source data generates the width, emoji, and
grapheme tables. Strings are decoded as Unicode scalar values and segmented by
extended grapheme-cluster rules. Combining and zero-width characters occupy no
columns; East Asian Wide and Fullwidth characters occupy two; Ambiguous values
occupy one; and fully-qualified flags, keycaps, presentation sequences, and
qualifying emoji ZWJ sequences occupy two columns per complete grapheme cluster.
ANSI terminal escape sequences remain ordinary input and are not removed.

## Migration

Existing imports can remain unchanged through the exact alias:

`wcwidth@npm:@stackline/wcwidth@1.0.0`

Downstreams should run a clean install and their ordinary tests, types, build,
and snapshot checks. Width snapshots containing emoji, combining text, CJK, or
post-Unicode-5 characters should receive focused review. This replacement is
independently maintained and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the original
project or the Unicode Consortium.
